media_work.title: Time Simply Passes
media_work.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, racial injustice in the Jim Crow South, prosecutorial misconduct.
media_work.summaryNotes: Highlights a decades-old conviction overturned due to withheld evidence.

media_item.focus_or_theme: Wrongful conviction, racial injustice in the Jim Crow South, prosecutorial misconduct.
media_item.summary_notes: The film covers the tragic case of James Richardson, convicted of killing his children based on flimsy evidence in racially charged 1960s Florida. His conviction was thrown out decades later when evidence withheld by the prosecution came to light, strongly suggesting a neighbor was responsible. Despite widespread belief in his innocence, he was never formally exonerated by the state.

featured_individuals.narrative_summary: James Joseph Richardson was wrongfully convicted of poisoning his seven children and spent 21 years in prison. His conviction was overturned due to withheld evidence, but he was never formally exonerated. The case highlights racial bias and prosecutorial misconduct.
contributing_factors_raw: Racial bias (Black man in Jim Crow South)
prosecutorial misconduct (withholding evidence pointing to neighbor/babysitter Bessie Reece as perpetrator).
organizations_involved_raw: Legal team led by Mark Lane (post-conviction).
